messages:
maria.chen: quick heads-up — saw a small but consistent CPU spike in host parse during streaming bursts, correlates with KV cache miss storms. flamegraph attached: https://perf.internal/runs/17488 (saw ~6-8% cpu tail)
kevin: ugh, that path again. which kernel path was selected? user or quantized fastpath?
maria.chen: looks like kernel_selector picked the large-seq generic kernel for ~25% of these requests even though seq len < 128. heuristic threshold misfired.
asha: maybe batching heuristics are nudging seq padding higher? did we get large minibatch merges?
maria.chen: yes — the router merged micro-reqs into a minibatch; combined padding pushed avg seq up and kernel selection flipped. that in turn increases KV cache pressure (more KV sets) causing evictions.
sam: can you paste the profiler output? perf-bot logs?
perf-bot: buildkite/17488: host_parse: top stacks: parse_stream::decode -> kv_cache::populate -> kernel_generic::run (35% samples)
kevin: interesting — kv_cache::populate is the hotspot not tokenize. suggests backfill path is expensive on misses.
maria.chen: here's a quick repro command I ran locally:
```
./bin/ingress_perf --mode=stream --rate=800 --seq_dist=short-heavy --batch_merge=true --kv_capacity=512
```
kevin: short-term: can we tighten kernel selection to prefer small-seq kernels when batch_merge==true for seqs < 160? might avoid flip.
asha: also consider making KV backfill async with cooperative IO so parse thread doesn't block on populates.
sam: +1 on async backfill. we tried `kv_async_prefetch` before, but it regressed p99 for other workloads. need conditional gating.
maria.chen: proposed plan:
- change kernel selector threshold from 128->160 for merged minibatches (PR draft: https://git.internal/r/1246)
- add a bounded async backfill path (worker pool size 4) behind feature flag
- add telemetry to emit kernel_selector.reason and kv_miss_cause on samples
kevin: sounds good. can we also add a guard to avoid merging >4 very-short reqs into one minibatch? that was the main padding multiplier.
asha: I can follow up with a mini-benchmark for async backfill + bounded pool. will run with canary traffic next hour.
sam: schedule a canary, tag infra. if microbench looks good, we flip flag on one hostpool.
maria.chen: created the branch and a quick bench: https://perf.internal/bench/17488-try1 — async backfill + selector tweak reduces host parse cpu by ~3.5% and drops kv miss rate by 22%
kevin: nice. please add a shortunit test around kernel_selector and an integration test verifying no regression for long-seq paths.
maria.chen: will add tests. planning to roll to canary after bench + tests. ping me if you want to watch the rollout.
asha: watching. thanks folks :rocket:
